slides.heading: Height Balanced Binary Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Height Balanced Binary Tree, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: For every node, do left/right subtree heights differ by at most 1?
Returns -1 from the helper as an "unbalanced" sentinel.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. For every node, do left or right subtree heights differ by at most 1? Returns -1 from the helper as an "unbalanced" sentinel.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Compute heights bottom-up and fail fast if any node's subtrees differ by more than one.
slides.narration: Compute heights bottom-up and fail fast if any node's subtrees differ by more than one.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: compute height separately at every node → O(n²)
Single post-order returning height or −1 → O(n)
slides.narration: Calling a separate height function at every node repeats work and is quadratic on skewed trees. A single post-order pass that returns the height, or minus one for unbalanced, checks everything in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, post-order returns height and balance. Second, compare child heights. Third, propagate any imbalance up.

slides.caption: Node 4: heights 0 and 0 → height 1
slides.narration: At node 4, the subtree heights are 0 and 0. That's balanced, with height 1.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The helper returns zero for null. It computes both child heights; if either is minus one or they differ by more than one, it returns minus one. Otherwise it returns one plus the larger.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Check every node, not just the root
slides.narration: An empty tree is balanced, and the condition must hold at every node, not just the root.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Return a small object instead of a sentinel
slides.narration: In a real codebase, return a small object with height and balanced flag. A follow-up is how AVL trees rebalance with rotations.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Compute heights bottom-up and fail fast if any node's subtrees differ by more than one.
slides.narration: To recap Height Balanced Binary Tree: Compute heights bottom-up and fail fast if any node's subtrees differ by more than one. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
